title: Data Platform Proof-of-Value: Kickoff Playbook and Acceptance Criteria
content:
Summary:

This is the kickoff playbook for a 6-week proof-of-value (PoV) with DataHub Inc. to validate Redwood Inference as the production inference layer for their internal data platform (semantic search + retrieval-augmented generation). The goal of the PoV is to demonstrate throughput, latency, cost, and retrieval quality at scale on a representative subset of DataHub’s content and to validate an operational runbook for deployment in Dedicated mode.

POV Objectives (top-level):
- Prove end-to-end semantic search (ingest -> embeddings -> ANN index -> query) on ~2M documents representative of DataHub production slices.
- Validate RAG pipeline for internal docs: relevance/precision at 1K live queries/day workload.
- Measure cost and latency at scale and provide optimizations (batching, caching, quantization) that meet customer SLOs.
- Produce an acceptance checklist and operations runbook for Dedicated deployment.

Scope / Not in scope:
- In scope: embeddings generation, index seeding (FAISS/HNSW), query-time reranking, small RAG demo app, perf/latency/cost profiling, canary rollout plan for Dedicated.
- Not in scope: full production migration, long-term retention/backups for index, model training/fine-tuning beyond simple prompt templates.

Success criteria (must have / nice to have):
- Must-have (quantitative):
  - Ingestion and embedding throughput: be able to create embeddings for 2M documents within 72 hours sustained (>=8k docs/min average ingest rate).
  - Query latency: 95th percentile end-to-end query latency (user query -> final answer from RAG) <= 350ms for single-response queries under expected load (1K q/day with short bursts to 200 q/min).
  - Retrieval quality: recall@10 >= 0.78 on the labeled testset and MRR >= 0.56.
  - Cost visibility: Per-query token cost and per-embedding cost measurements available with breakdowns by model, batching, and infra.
  - Reliability: System maintains >= 99.5% successful request rate during a 72-hour soak at target load.

- Nice-to-have (qualitative / stretch):
  - Reduced tail latency: 99th percentile < 800ms with caching enabled.
  - Demo app: integrated search UI with feedback loop for re-ranking and simple analytics.
  - Ops: Playbook for automated rollbacks and model-variant fallbacks.

Acceptance tests (concrete pass/fail checks):
1) Ingest pipeline test:
   - Input: 100k document ingest batch representative of production mix.
   - Check: All documents receive embeddings and are indexed; errors < 0.1% and retries succeed for transient failures.
   - Pass criteria: Completion within 90 minutes for 100k (scales up to 2M in 72 hours).

2) Query load test:
   - Input: Simulated traffic of 1,000 q/day with bursts to 200 q/min for 10 minutes every hour for 12 hours.
   - Check: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 350ms; error rate < 0.5%.

3) Retrieval quality test:
   - Input: Labeled 500-query testset from customer with human-annotated relevancy judgments.
   - Check: recall@10, MRR meet must-have thresholds.

4) Observability + cost reporting:
   - Check: Per-route dashboards exist for embeddings and generation with token-level breakdown, and cost estimates per 10k queries.

5) Security/access test:
   - Check: VPC peering (or dedicated private connectivity) validated; secret injection via customer KMS tested in staging.

Milestones & timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff, owner: SE lead): data sample selection, access onboarding, staging environment provisioned.
- Week 1: Ingest pipeline + sample indexing, baseline embedding model selection.
- Week 2: Query integration + initial latency profiling, build small RAG demo.
- Week 3: Load testing + cost profiling, iterate on batching and caching.
- Week 4: Dedicated deployment dry-run in staging, failover test, SLO verification.
- Week 5: User acceptance testing with customer SMEs, collect qualitative feedback.
- Week 6: Final acceptance report, handoff runbook and next-step proposal.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood PoV Lead: Priya Kaur (owner) - overall coordination, customer alignment, acceptance sign-off.
- Solutions Engineer: Ethan Liu - ingestion, indexing, query integration, demo app.
- Infra/Platform: Connor Hayes - staging infra provisioning, Dedicated dry-run, networking.
- Customer PM/SME: Mariana Ortiz - data access, testset curation, UAT coordination.
- Observability SME: Elena Smirnova - dashboards, cost reports, tracing hooks.

Prereqs / Access checklist for Week 0 (must be completed before kickoff):
- Data sample: 100k representative documents (s3 link or GDrive export).
- Credentials: VPN/VPC peering details or temporary upload bucket, KMS test key, API allowlist for Redwood staging accounts.
- Testset: 500 labeled queries + relevance judgments.
- Stakeholders: Weekly 30-min sync recurring calendar invite with customer PM, security lead, and SEs.

Workshop agenda (kickoff + technical deep dive, 90 minutes):
- 0-10m: Introductions, goals and success criteria alignment.
- 10-30m: Data & access review (customer outlines data mix, legal/security concerns).
- 30-50m: Redwood arch review (ingest, embeddings, index, RAG flow, Dedicated options).
- 50-70m: Operational requirements (SLOs, alerting, backup, KMS, audit logs).
- 70-85m: Implementation plan and timeline, responsibilities.
- 85-90m: Q&A and immediate next steps.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customer data includes large binary assets and inconsistent schema -> Mitigation: Provide lightweight preprocessing rules, sample normalization scripts, and early data profiling within first 48 hours.
- Risk: Tail latency spikes under burst -> Mitigation: Enable prefix caching and model-variant routing for fallbacks; set canary limits.
- Risk: Security clearance delays -> Mitigation: Offer temporary sanitized dataset and run tests in Redwood staging with redacted PII.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Ingest: chunking strategy, retry policy, backpressure controls.
- Embeddings: recommended model variants for accuracy/cost tradeoffs; batching recommendations (optimize for throughput during bulk index vs. single-document ingestion).
- Indexing: HNSW parameters for recall/latency tradeoff; reindex window and snapshot cadence.
- Query serving: continuous batching knobs, prefix cache TTL defaults, fallback routing config.
- Monitoring: dashboards to ship (token cost, per-route latency, error budget burn-down, index health).

Acceptance sign-off process:
- SE and Customer PM jointly verify acceptance tests and produce a short acceptance report.
- Required signatures: Customer PM (Mariana Ortiz), Redwood PoV Lead (Priya Kaur), Redwood Platform (Connor Hayes).

Deliverables at PoV close:
- Acceptance report with test logs and perf graphs.
- Cost model spreadsheet showing per-10k queries and index costs for production scale.
- Step-by-step Dedicated deployment runbook and rollback plan.
- Demo app + source link and quickstart README.

Open questions to resolve in kickoff:
- Exact production shard sizing for indices and whether customer will keep index in their cloud or in Redwood-managed infra.
- Final choice of embedding model (customer prefers open model: which of our verified catalog variants is acceptable?).
- Regulatory requirements for logs retention and PII handling.

Immediate next steps (within 48 hours):
1) Confirm data-sample upload and share testset (owner: Mariana).
2) Provide staging network/KMS details (owner: Customer infra).
3) SEs to provision staging infra and run a 10k doc ingest smoke test (owner: Ethan).
4) Schedule kickoff workshop invite with calendar and dial-in (owner: Priya).

Notes / informal:
- Keep experiment iterations small and measurable—prefer quantitative A/B between model variants rather than open-ended tuning sessions.
- For the demo, prioritize the developer UX (clear request/response timings) over fancy UI features.
- Log all transient errors to a shared slack channel #pov-datahub for rapid triage.

Contact info (preferred):
- Priya Kaur (PoV lead) — priya@redwood.ai 
- Ethan Liu (SE) — ethan@redwood.ai
- Connor Hayes (Platform) — connor@redwood.ai

End of document.
